$ xref live trace

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options
  3. Examples
  4. What one call of a hot function does
  5. Reading the output
  6. Limits
  7. Provenance

Record what a thread does between two points: each time a thread enters a --start function, xref opens a window for that thread and records, in order, the entries and returns of the traced functions until the window closes (--stop-return of the start function, or --stop at an address). --callees-of traces every static call site of a function, so one command shows what it calls and in which order. Uses Linux tracefs uprobes.

Usage

xref live trace [OPTIONS] --pid <PID> --start <VA>

Arguments and options

Options

--pid <PID>
Target process ID (must be non-zero).
--start <VA>
Start address opening a thread-scoped trace window (0x... hex or decimal; repeatable).
--start-filter <PRED>
Numeric predicate gating window creation on --start fetches (FIELD <OP> INTEGER; repeatable).
--stop-return <VA>
Close an active window on the matching return of this --start function (0x... or decimal).
--stop <VA>
Close an active window when its thread reaches this address (0x... or decimal).
--functions <VA>
Comma-separated or repeated function entry addresses to trace (VA,VA,...).
--callees-of <FN>
Expand static call sites and post-call return sites from function FN (0x... or symbol).
--depth <N>
Static callee expansion depth for --callees-of (1..=16, defaults to 1).
--fetch <NAME=EXPR>
Fetch expression(s) attached to --start probes (NAME=EXPR[,NAME=EXPR...]).
--fetch-at <VA> <NAME=EXPR,...>
Attach entry/call-site fetch expressions at VA (--fetch-at VA "NAME=EXPR,...").
--fetch-ret <VA> <NAME=EXPR,...>
Attach return fetch expressions for VA (--fetch-ret VA "NAME=EXPR,...").
--max-windows <N>
Stop and detach after completing this many trace windows (1..=4096).
--max-events <N>
Stop and detach after recording this many trace events (1..=65536).
--duration-ms <MS>
Observation duration in milliseconds (0 runs until limits, target exit, or SIGINT).
--force-bin
Rejects unverified binary mismatches; accepted for CLI symmetry with other live commands.
--json
Emit structured schema_version: 1 JSON output.

Examples

The target is ripgrep 14.1.1 (rg) filtering an endless input stream, as on live maps. PIDs and runtime addresses belong to that run.

What one call of a hot function does

Command
$ sudo xref -b rg live trace --pid 4140799 --start 0x430060 --stop-return 0x430060 --callees-of 0x430060 --max-windows 2 --duration-ms 1000
Output
pid 4140799  match verified_sha256  slide +0x707697000000  backend tracefs  return_mode mixed_uretprobe_best_effort
warning: uretprobe_returns_are_best_effort_under_unwind
window 1  tid 4140799  start 0x430060  status complete  stop 0x430060
   0  > 0x430060 @0x138f62
   1    > 0x4307b0 @0x430070
   1    < 0x4307b0
   1    > 0x4302b0 @0x430087
   1    < 0x4302b0
   0  < 0x430060
window 2  tid 4140799  start 0x430060  status complete  stop 0x430060
   0  > 0x430060 @0x138f62
   1    > 0x4307b0 @0x430070
   1    < 0x4307b0
   1    > 0x4302b0 @0x430087
   1    < 0x4302b0
   0  < 0x430060
summary: windows=2 events=12 lost=0 stop=max_windows elapsed_ms=11
stderr
xref: probe_ready {"backend":"tracefs","pid":4140799,"attached_tids":[4140799],"probes":["0x430060","0x430070","0x430076","0x430087","0x43008d","0x4300c1","0x4300c7","0x4300de","0x4300e3","0x4300e6","0x430060"],"tracefs_instance":"xref_trace_4140799_003f2f07a47c23ab","uprobe_events":["xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_0","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_1","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_2","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_3","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_4","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_5","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_6","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_7","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_8","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_9","xt_003f2f07a47c23ab/xt_003f2f07a47c23ab_10"]}

Reading the output

  • probe_ready on stderr lists every probe and the private tracefs instance; the instance is removed when the command ends.
  • Each window is one thread's run from start to stop. Rows are depth, > entry or < return, the function, and for entries the call site (@). Here both windows show the same sequence: 0x430060 calls 0x4307b0, then 0x4302b0, and returns.
  • summary: windows and events recorded, lost events, why it stopped.

Limits

  • Needs root (tracefs uprobes).
  • Returns are recorded with uretprobes, which are best effort when the stack is unwound by panics or longjmp; the warning says so.
  • Windows are per thread; calls on other threads do not appear in them.

Provenance

Recorded with xref 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Live examples ran against one ripgrep process filtering an endless input stream; commands shown with sudo ran as root. Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
